keyVerseText: And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron's heart, when he goeth in before the LORD: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the LORD continually.
rootMeaning: The root of תֻּמִּים (Tummîym) is תֹּם (tôm), which conveys ideas of completeness, integrity, and moral innocence. This root suggests a state of being whole and unblemished, emphasizing purity and uprightness rather than mere flawlessness. The plural form תֻּמִּים thus carries the sense of multiple aspects or expressions of perfection and integrity, highlighting a comprehensive wholeness that goes beyond a simple English translation of "perfection."
usageInScripture: The term תֻּמִּים appears five times in Scripture, consistently associated with the Urim and used in the context of the high priest's breastplate. Translations such as "and the Thummim" and "Let thy Thummim" reveal its role as an object or emblem connected to divine revelation and judgment. This consistent usage underscores its technical and sacred function as a means to discern God's will, emphasizing complete truth and moral integrity in decision-making.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding תֻּמִּים as emblematic of perfection and integrity enriches our grasp of God's holiness and truth. It signifies not only an external symbol on the high priest's breastplate but also a divine standard of moral completeness that believers are called to pursue. The connection with the Urim and the revelation of God's will reminds us that true guidance and judgment come from God's perfect truth. This word thus points to Christ, who embodies perfect righteousness and is the ultimate source of divine revelation and moral purity for the believer.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 28:30 instructs placing the Urim and the Thummim in the breastplate of judgment so that Aaron may bear the judgment of Israel continually before the LORD. The word תֻּמִּים here highlights the role of these objects as instruments of perfect truth and integrity, ensuring that the high priest carries God's complete and holy judgment. This conveys the seriousness and sacredness of representing God's will, reminding us that God's judgments are grounded in perfect truth and moral completeness.
